new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-06-13 (Governor Katie Hobbs signed HB 4168, enacted as Chapter 140); the Section 31 application freeze runs 2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30
new_candidates.duration: Three-year bar (2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30) on the Arizona Commerce Authority accepting new applications for the A.R.S. 41-1519 computer data center tax-relief program; applies retroactively from after 2026-06-30 and is repealed after 2029-06-30
new_candidates.legal_basis: HB 4168, Section 31, enacted as 2026 Arizona Session Laws Chapter 140
new_candidates.trigger: Statewide pause on new applications to the A.R.S. 41-1519 data center tax-relief program, adopted amid a legislative session dominated by data center issues
new_candidates.current_status: In effect as of 2026-07-01. The Arizona Commerce Authority reportedly received 113 tax-relief applications between 2026-06-15 and 2026-06-30, immediately before the freeze took effect; those applications still required approval or denial. Governor Hobbs distinguished the measure from a construction or permitting moratorium in July 7 remarks.

evidence.supports: Full enacted text of HB 4168/Chapter 140, Section 31, barring new A.R.S. 41-1519 data center tax-relief applications from 2026-07-01 through 2029-06-30
Describes the enacted three-year data center tax-incentive application pause
Reports 113 applications filed between June 15-30, 2026 immediately before the freeze, and clarifies the scope of the pause versus construction/permitting

new_candidates.notes: IMPORTANT SCOPING FLAG: this is a moratorium on NEW APPLICATIONS to a state tax-incentive program (A.R.S. 41-1519), not a pause on data center construction, siting, or local land-use/permitting approvals -- Governor Hobbs and reporting both make this distinction explicitly. Included because it is the only 'Moratorium vote' tagged action identified anywhere in Arizona across the May-July 2026 chronology sweep, and Arizona currently has zero rows in the inventory, so this is Arizona's first candidate under this research pass. No city- or county-level data center construction/permitting moratorium was identified in Arizona during this period; Flagstaff, Tucson, Pima County, Marana, Pinal County, and Casa Grande all had active data center land-use disputes in May-July 2026 but none had enacted a moratorium as of 2026-07-31 (Tucson and Pima County were drafting permanent zoning standards, not pausing approvals; Pinal County continued rezoning cases without recommendation; Casa Grande was processing a Prop 207 claim).
